questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to start an online bookshop from your garage
How Jeff Bezos thinks and how Amazon became a success
Why online shopping is bad for small shops in towns
The history of space exploration and rocket travel
questions.why: Neil says they'll look inside the brain of Jeff Bezos to find out how he thinks.

questions.q: Which three words do Bezos's friends often use to describe him?
options: Kind, funny and generous to everyone
Shy, careful and extremely hard-working
Rich, famous and powerful in business
Invention, risk-taking and long-term vision
questions.why: Georgina says friends often use 'invention, risk-taking and long-term vision'.

questions.q: What did Bezos's grandfather teach him?
options: That careful thinking can solve any problem
That money is the most important thing
That books are better than cars
That taking risks is dangerous
questions.why: Neil says Lawrence taught Jeff that by careful thinking, any problem can be solved.

questions.q: Why does Bezos compare Amazon to the old truck?
options: Because both were cheap to buy at the time
Because both often broke down
Both are heavy but unstoppable once moving
Because both belonged to his grandfather
questions.why: He compares Amazon to the truck: very heavy, but impossible to stop when it rolls downhill.

questions.q: According to Natalie Berg, what is the key to Amazon's success?
options: Having the lowest prices from the start
Putting customers at the centre of the business
Selling only books
Spending a lot on advertising
questions.why: She says Bezos was relentlessly focusing on customers and putting them at the heart of the business.

questions.q: What happened after Bezos started Market Place?
options: More sellers brought more customers and lower prices
Amazon stopped selling its own products
Prices went up for customers
Amazon lost money during the Covid pandemic
questions.why: Georgina says more sellers brought more customers, which in turn brought down prices.

questions.q: According to Tom Rivett-Carnac, why is Bezos interested in climate change?
options: He wants to make much more money from green technology
His grandfather asked him to protect the planet
He wants to be remembered for doing the right thing
The US government forced Amazon to cut its emissions
questions.why: He says it seemed a legacy issue: Bezos wanted to be on the right side of history.

questions.q: What does Tom Rivett-Carnac think about companies acting to improve their reputation?
options: It is always a form of greenwashing
It should be against the law
It never achieves anything
It's fine if they achieve something real
questions.why: He says 'that is fine', as long as they do something meaningful and deliver a major outcome.
